newsitem.title: USA: Stocks stage broad rally ahead of jobs report.
newsitem.headline: Stocks stage broad rally ahead of jobs report.

text.p: Stocks finished broadly higher on Thursday in a surprising show of investor confidence ahead of a key monthly U.S. employment report.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 35.63 points to 7,305.29.
In the broader market, advances outpaced declines 1,489 to 957 on volume of 452.6 million on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index gained 10.38 points to 1,390.05.
The broad rally, which first lifted technology stocks but spread quickly to financials, transportation stocks and other sectors, came as a surprise to many on Wall Street.
"It's definitely intriguing the market has the confidence to run up ahead of the employment number," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
"This seems to be a bet on a benign number," he said.
The employment report for May is due Friday morning. Nonfarm payrolls are expected to show a 219,000 gain during the month.

Stocks got little support from the bond market, where the yield on the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury was unchanged at 6.88 percent. Also, stock market volume was relatively light, indicating many investors were holding fire on Thursday.
Even so, the session's decidedly upward bias, which saw the Dow rally as many as 80 points, raised eyebrows.
"I certainly wouldn't have guessed today would be the best day of the week," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
One possibility, said Acuff, was that investors had shaken some of the earnings jitters that arose after a flurry of warnings starting last Friday with Intel Corp.
"It looks like the concern this week may really have been about earnings," he said. "Investors may have decided the issues were limited to individual companies."
Technology stocks turned in a particularly solid showing, rebounding after their recent downturn.
Microsoft Corp. rose 1-3/8 to 120-9/16, Dell Computer Corp. gained 3-11/16 to 108-7/16 and Intel climbed 41/64 to 143-9/64.

"Given what we saw earlier this week, today looked like a bargain hunter's bounce in the tech area," said Charles White, managing director at Avatar Associates. "Intel, for one, is still more than 20 points off its high."

Whether the bounce has any staying power will depend for the near term on the outcome of Friday's employment report, the last such report the Federal Reserve will see before its interest rate policy meeting in early July.
Fisher Scientific International Inc. surged 7-1/2 to 45-3/8 after the instrument and equipment maker received a recapitalization offer from Trinity I Fund LP.

According to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the offer values Fisher at "perhaps in the range of $47 to $48 per share." Trinity, which owns 10.6 percent of Fisher, said it would also consider a cash merger.

Factory Card Outlet Corp. skidded 3-1/16 to 5-13/16. The company warned Wednesday that earnings for the fourth quarter would be lower than expected. Alex. Brown & Sons downgraded the shares to buy from strong buy.

UCAR International Inc. tumbled 6-3/8 to 41-7/8. The company said it was served with a U.S. grand jury subpoena and search warrant relating to an investigation of possible price-fixing by producers of graphite electrodes.
UCAR, the world's largest maker of graphite and carbon electrodes, said it was co-operating with the investigation.
Shares in UCAR competitor SGL Carbon AG fell 4-3/4 to 46 before a trading halt late in the morning. The shares did not resume trading.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 3.32 points to 843.43. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 3.02 to 610.75.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.46 to 441.64. The average price per share rose 14 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues also known as the Wilshire 5000 -- was 8,026.563, up 32.570, or 0.141 percent.
